title: Pitfall II: Lost Caverns
subtitle: Harry descends into the caverns
summary: Pitfall II: Lost Caverns is David Crane's 1984 sequel to Pitfall!, published by Activision for the Atari 2600.
body: Pitfall II: Lost Caverns is David Crane's 1984 sequel to Pitfall!, published by Activision for the Atari 2600. Harry explores caverns in Peru to recover the Raj diamond and rescue Rhonda and Quickclaw. The adventure expands down through ladders, tunnels and water, with balloons offering another way to travel. Finding the next passage matters alongside avoiding its inhabitants. The player gradually learns how the underground spaces connect, turning a series of short movements into a longer expedition through one continuous environment.

Red crosses mark places to which Harry returns after an accident. A collision costs points and sends him back to the last checkpoint, making the score reflect the care taken along the route. Gold bars reward exploration, while swimming and balloon travel change how a passage must be approached. The structure encourages another attempt at a troublesome section: the player keeps the knowledge gained about the caverns and can apply it immediately. Progress depends on understanding where to go as much as executing an individual jump.

Crane designed a Display Processor Chip for the cartridge to extend the aging console's capabilities. It supported richer graphics and a dedicated music circuit, allowing a more elaborate expedition than the earlier game. The technological work serves a visible purpose in the adventure's larger spaces and continuing musical accompaniment. Rhonda and Quickclaw also carried characters from the Pitfall television cartoon into the game. Pitfall II brought hardware, exploration and familiar characters together around an increasingly ambitious journey for Atari's machine.
